readings.title: Remembering the Exodus
readings.subtitle: Forty Years in the Wilderness
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 29:1] These are the words of the covenant which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh to make with <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl in the land of Mo’aḇ, besides the covenant which <dn>He</dn> made with <dn>את</dn> them in Ḥorěḇ. [2] And Mosheh called all Yisra’ěl and said to them, “You yourselves saw <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did before your eyes in the land of Mitsrayim, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land. [3] “Your eyes saw <dn>את</dn> the great trials, <dn>את</dn> the signs, and <dn>את</dn> those great wonders. [4] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not given you a heart to know and eyes to see and ears to hear, till this day. [5] “And <dn>I</dn> have led <dn>את</dn> you forty years in the wilderness. Your garments have not worn out on you, and your sandals have not worn out on your feet. [6] “You ate no bread and drank no wine nor strong drink, so that you might know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [7] “And when you came to this place, Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon and Oḡ sovereign of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we struck <dn>את</dn> them, [8] and took <dn>את</dn> their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Re’uḇěnites, and to the Gaḏites, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh. [9] “Therefore you shall guard <dn>את</dn> the words of this covenant, and do <dn>את</dn> them, so that you prosper in <dn>את</dn> all that you do.

readings.title: Standing Before the Creator
readings.subtitle: Establishing the People
readings.text: [10] “All of you are standing today before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>: your leaders, your tribes, your elders and your officers, all the men of Yisra’ěl, [11] your little ones, your wives, and your sojourner who is in the midst of your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water, [12] so that you should enter into covenant with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and into <dn>His</dn> oath, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> makes with you today, [13] in order to establish <dn>את</dn> you today as a people for <dn>Himself</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to you, and as <dn>He</dn> has sworn to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ. [14] “And not with <dn>את</dn> you alone <dn>I</dn> am making <dn>את</dn> this covenant and <dn>את</dn> this oath, [15] but with <dn>את</dn> him who stands here with us today before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, as well as with <dn>את</dn> him who is not here with us today.

readings.title: The Root of Bitterness
readings.subtitle: The Plagues of Disobedience
readings.text: [16] “For you know <dn>את</dn> how we dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim and <dn>את</dn> how we passed through the nations which you passed through, [17] and you saw <dn>את</dn> their abominations and <dn>את</dn> their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were with them, [18] lest there should be among you a man or woman or clan or tribe, whose heart turns away today from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to go and serve <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of these nations, lest there should be among you a root bearing bitterness or wormwood. [19] “And it shall be, when he hears <dn>את</dn> the words of this curse, that he should bless himself in his heart, saying, ‘I have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ in order to add drunkenness to thirst. [20] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would not forgive him, but rather, the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>His</dn> jealousy shall burn against that man, and every curse that is written in this book shall settle on him, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall blot out <dn>את</dn> his name from under the heavens. [21] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall separate him for evil, out of all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, according to all the curses of the covenant that are written in this Book of the Torah. [22] “And the generation to come of your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a far land, shall say when they see <dn>את</dn> the plagues of that land and <dn>את</dn> the sicknesses which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent into it: [23] All its land is sulphur, salt, and burning; it is not sown, nor does it bear, nor does any grass grow there, like the overthrow of Seḏom and Amorah, Aḏmah and Tseḇoyim, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> overthrew in <dn>His</dn> displeasure and <dn>His</dn> wrath.’ [24] “And all nations shall say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done so to this land? What does the heat of this great displeasure mean?’ [25] “And it shall be said, ‘Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, which <dn>He</dn> made with them when <dn>He</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> them out of the land of Mitsrayim. [26] And they went and served other mighty ones and bowed themselves to them, mighty ones that they did not know and that <dn>He</dn> had not given to them, [27] therefore the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against this land, to bring on it <dn>את</dn> every curse that is written in this book. [28] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> uprooted them from their land in displeasure, and in wrath, and in great rage, and cast them into another land, as it is today.’ [29] “The secret matters belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, but what is revealed belongs to us and to our children forever, to do <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah.

readings.title: Turning Back from Captivity
readings.subtitle: Compassion and Gathering
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 30:1] “And it shall be, when all these words come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before you, and you shall bring them back to your heart among all the nations where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> drives you, [2] and shall turn back to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and obey <dn>His</dn> voice, according to all that I command you today, with all your heart and with all your being, you and your children, [3] then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> your captivity, and shall have compassion on you, and <dn>He</dn> shall turn back and gather you from all the peoples where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has scattered you. [4] “If any of you are driven out to the farthest parts under the heavens, from there <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does gather you, and from there <dn>He</dn> does take you. [5] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bring you to the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it. And <dn>He</dn> shall do good to you, and increase you more than your fathers. [6] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall circumcise <dn>את</dn> your heart and <dn>את</dn> the heart of your seed, to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with all your heart and with all your being, so that you might live, [7] and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall put <dn>את</dn> all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you. [8] “And you shall turn back and obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands which I command you today. [9] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall make you have excess in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground for good. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turns back to rejoice over you for good as <dn>He</dn> rejoiced over your fathers, [10] if you obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws which are written in this Book of the Torah, if you turn back to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with all your heart and with all your being.

readings.title: The Word is Near
readings.subtitle: Blessing and Curse Set Before You
readings.text: [11] “For this command which I am commanding you today, it is not too hard for you, nor is it far off. [12] “It is not in the heavens, to say, ‘Who shall ascend into the heavens for us, and bring it to us, and cause us to hear <dn>את</dn> it, so that we do it?’ [13] “Nor is it beyond the sea, to say, ‘Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and cause us to hear <dn>את</dn> it, so that we do it?’ [14] “For the Word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart – to do it. [15] “See, I have set before you today <dn>את</dn> life and <dn>את</dn> good, and <dn>את</dn> death and <dn>את</dn> evil, [16] in that I am commanding you today to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways, and to guard <dn>His</dn> commands, and <dn>His</dn> laws, and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings. And you shall live and increase, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bless you in the land which you go to possess. [17] “But if your heart turns away, and you do not obey, and shall be drawn away, and shall bow down to other mighty ones and serve them, [18] “I have declared to you today that you shall certainly perish, you shall not prolong your days in the land which you are passing over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn to enter and possess. [19] “I have called <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth as witnesses today against you: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore you shall choose life, so that you live, both you and your seed, [20] to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to obey <dn>His</dn> voice, and to cling to <dn>Him</dn> – for <dn>He</dn> is your life and the length of your days – to dwell in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ, to give them.”

readings.title: Passing Over the Jordan
readings.subtitle: Be Strong and Courageous
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 31:1] And Mosheh went and spoke <dn>את</dn> these words to all Yisra’ěl, [2] and he said to them, “I am one hundred and twenty years old today. I am no longer able to go out and come in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to me, ‘You do not pass over <dn>את</dn> this Yarděn.’ [3] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> is passing over before you. <dn>He</dn> shall destroy <dn>את</dn> these nations from before you and you possess them. Yehoshua himself is passing over before you, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken. [4] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall do to them as <dn>He</dn> did to Siḥon and to Oḡ, the sovereigns of the Amorites and their land, when <dn>He</dn> destroyed <dn>את</dn> them. [5] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give them over to you, and you shall do to them according to all the command which I have commanded <dn>את</dn> you. [6] “Be strong and courageous, do not fear nor be afraid of them. For it is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> who is going with you. <dn>He</dn> does not fail you nor forsake you.” [7] And Mosheh called Yehoshua and said to him before the eyes of all Yisra’ěl, “Be strong and courageous, for you are going with <dn>את</dn> this people to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn to their fathers to give them, and you are to let them inherit it. [8] “And it is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who is going before you, <dn>He</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> is with you. <dn>He</dn> does not fail you nor forsake you. Do not fear nor be discouraged.”

readings.subsection: The Public Reading of the Torah
readings.title: The Festival of Sukkot
readings.subtitle: Assembling the People
readings.text: [9] And Mosheh wrote <dn>את</dn> this Torah and gave it to the priests, the sons of Lěvi, who bore <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and to all the elders of Yisra’ěl. [10] And Mosheh commanded them, saying, “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time, the year of release, at the Festival of Sukkot, [11] when all Yisra’ěl comes to appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the place which <dn>He</dn> chooses, read <dn>את</dn> this Torah before all Yisra’ěl in their hearing. [12] “Assemble <dn>את</dn> the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your sojourner who is within your gates, so that they hear, and so that they learn to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and guard to do <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah. [13] “And their children, who have not known it, should hear and learn to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> as long as you live in the land you are passing over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn to possess.”

readings.title: The Tent of Appointment
readings.subtitle: Foretelling the Rebellion
readings.text: [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, the days have drawn near for you to die. Call <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Appointment, so that <dn>I</dn> command him.”</dq> And Mosheh and Yehoshua went and presented themselves in the Tent of Appointment. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared at the Tent in a column of a cloud, and the column of a cloud stood above the door of the Tent. [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, you are about to sleep with your fathers. And this people shall rise and whore after the mighty ones of the strangers of the land into the midst of which they shall enter, and forsake <dn>Me</dn> and break <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant which <dn>I</dn> have made with them.</dq> [17] <dq>“Then <dn>My</dn> displeasure shall burn against them in that day, and <dn>I</dn> shall forsake them and hide <dn>My</dn> face from them, and they shall be consumed. And many evils and distresses shall come upon them, and it shall be said in that day, ‘Is it not because our <dn>Elohim</dn> is not in our midst that these evils have come upon us?’</dq> [18] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall certainly hide <dn>My</dn> face in that day, because of all the evil which they have done, for they shall turn to other mighty ones.</dq> [19] <dq>“And now write down <dn>את</dn> this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Yisra’ěl. Put it in their mouths, so that this song is to <dn>Me</dn> for a witness against the children of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [20] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring them to the land flowing with milk and honey, of which <dn>I</dn> swore to their fathers, and they shall eat and be satisfied and be fat, then they shall turn to other mighty ones, and they shall serve them, and scorn <dn>Me</dn> and break <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant.</dq> [21] <dq>“And it shall be, when many evils and distresses come upon them, that this song shall answer before them as a witness. For it is not to be forgotten in the mouths of their seed, for <dn>I</dn> know <dn>את</dn> their thoughts which they are forming today, even before <dn>I</dn> bring them to the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to give them.”</dq> [22] And Mosheh wrote <dn>את</dn> this song the same day, and taught it to the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Book Beside the Ark
readings.subtitle: The Stiff-Necked Generation
readings.text: [23] And <dn>He</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua son of Nun, and said, <dq>“Be strong and courageous, for you are to bring <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl into the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to them, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> am with you.”</dq> [24] And it came to be, when Mosheh had completed writing <dn>את</dn> the Words of this Torah in a book, until their completion, [25] that Mosheh commanded <dn>את</dn> the Lěvites, who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [26] “Take <dn>את</dn> this Book of the Torah, and you shall place <dn>את</dn> it beside the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and it shall be there as a witness against you, [27] for I myself know <dn>את</dn> your rebellion and <dn>את</dn> your stiff neck. See, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then how much more after my death? [28] “Assemble unto me <dn>את</dn> all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, so that I speak <dn>את</dn> these words in their hearing and call <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth to witness against them. [29] “For I know that after my death you shall do very corruptly and turn aside from the way which I have commanded <dn>את</dn> you. And evil shall come to <dn>את</dn> you in the latter days, because you do <dn>את</dn> what is evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to provoke <dn>Him</dn> through the work of your hands.” [30] So Mosheh spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Yisra’ěl <dn>את</dn> the words of this song till their completion:
